Test an MCP server.

Nine phases, 131 checks, both protocol generations. Every finding is tied to the request that produced it, and the whole run happens here — the endpoint, the credentials and the report never leave this machine.

Connect

Where to look, and what to authenticate with. Both the handshake revisions and 2026-07-28 are detected from the server itself — there is nothing to choose.

The Streamable HTTP URL. Five of the 131 checks apply only to a server that is a program rather than a URL; run those from the command line with passmcp check --stdio -- <command>.

A name, not a token.

The browser sends the variable's name. passmcp reads the value on this machine, uses it against the server you named, and never writes it into the report. Nothing here reaches anybody else's infrastructure.

Safety

Only tools declaring readOnlyHint are called. Everything here is an explicit opt-in, and belongs to a server you own.

Safety opt-ins

Tools

The same selector passmcp check -i draws in a terminal. Choosing a tool is an explicit opt-in, so picking a mutating one widens the policy for that tool and nothing else.

Tools to exercise

With nothing selected, every tool the policy already permits is exercised, which is what a run does by default.

Pacing

A scheduled diagnostic against somebody's production server is a load test if you let it be.

0 removes the throttle.
